newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse media profit falls in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse media profit falls in Q2.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp said Monday that operating profit in its media group fell almost 20 percent to $155 million from $192 million in the second quarter.

Total media sales rose nearly 17 percent to $1.28 billion from $1.10 billion in the period. The business reported EBITDA -- or earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization -- of $261 million compared with $340 million.
CBS Radio posted EBITDA of $157 million, about 23 percent above a year ago on a proforma basis.

Television station revenues declined four percent on a comparable station basis, and EBITDA was essentially flat. "We expect our ongoing growth, particularly in the major markets, to benefit significantly from greater interaction among our television, radio and outdoor businesses," said Michael Jordan, chairman and chief executive officer.
During the quarter, the company combined radio and television groups into a consolidated CBS Station Group and took several steps to improve advertising sales in its local markets.

At the TV network, EBITDA decreased significantly, primarily due to the effect of purchase price accounting and higher programming costs. Although key demographics have declined slightly, the network is continuing to grow audience share, it said.
It recorded revenues in its Power Systems business of $838 million versus $732 million and squeezed out operating profits of $1 million versus a loss of $35 million.
The Thermo King unit posted operating profits of $49 million and revenues of $263 million versus $46 million and $265 million.
